sections.title: About me
paragraphs: I am Valeria Stănculea, a clinical psychologist and relational integrative psychotherapist, licensed to practise by the Romanian College of Psychologists, specialising in work with children, adolescents, parents, and families. My work combines clinical assessment and psychological counselling with different forms of relational integrative intervention.
I also contribute to psychoeducation and prevention in mental health, and to the professional development of psychologists, trainee psychotherapists, and students.

In my work, professional training and clinical experience meet a calm, authentic, and approachable presence. I want the people I work with to feel heard, respected, and understood, without judgement or pressure to find every answer immediately.
Beyond my professional role, I am a wife and a parent. These roles are part of my life and help me remain connected to the concrete, complex, and often imperfect reality of family relationships.

I work responsibly and collaboratively, using scientifically grounded interventions within clear professional boundaries. For me, competence means not only knowledge and techniques, but also remaining attentive to each person's and family's story, pace, limits, and needs.

sections.title: What defines me professionally
paragraphs: I chose to work with children and families because I believe a child's development cannot be understood separately from the relationships and systems in which they live. Their behaviours, emotions, and difficulties make sense when considered alongside their developmental stage, experiences, and important relationships.
I therefore understand the child, parents, parent–child relationship, and family as interdependent parts of the same relational context.
I work authentically, collaboratively, and with balance. I do not pursue the image of a perfect professional or believe in universal solutions for every family.
I take professional responsibility for building relationships based on trust, respect, clarity, and boundaries, while remaining open to the uniqueness of each situation.
For me, change means more than reducing a behaviour or symptom. It also means developing the child's resources, supporting parents, and building safer, more functional family relationships.

sections.title: How I work
paragraphs: Every child and family has their own story. Before looking for solutions, I want to understand the child, parents, and context in which the difficulties arose as well as possible.
My practice starts with observation, listening, assessment, and understanding before intervention. I do not believe in universal recipes or solutions that fit every family.

Together with the child and parents, we gradually build more adaptive and functional ways of responding to challenges, developing resources and skills that support the child's development and the balance of the whole family.

I understand the child within their development and relationships. I consider the child or adolescent, parents, parent–child relationship, and family dynamics, without reducing difficulties to a single behaviour, symptom, or family member.

Collaboration with parents is an important part of the process. Parents are partners in understanding the child's difficulties and supporting changes in everyday life; I also attend to their own needs, resources, limits, and experiences.
The process begins with assessment of the situation and clarification of the child's and family's needs. On this basis, we agree on goals and appropriate support.
Intervention may include work with the child or adolescent, meetings with parents, work on the parent–child relationship, or family dynamics.
I work within a framework of safety, respect, collaboration, and clear professional boundaries. I seek balance between emotion and reason, acceptance and change, and the child's and parents' needs.
Interventions are scientifically grounded and adapted as the work progresses, according to the child's development and the family's needs.

sections.title: My mission
paragraphs: I contribute to children's healthy development and families' balance through clinical assessment, psychotherapeutic intervention, education, and prevention in mental health.
I believe in the power of relationships and want to support parents and families, as well as professionals who contribute to children's growth and development.

sections.title: Beyond clinical practice
paragraphs: Direct clinical work with children, adolescents, parents, and families remains the centre of my work. At the same time, I believe supporting mental health extends beyond individual intervention in the practice.

Psychoeducation and prevention are an important direction of my work. I want to contribute to clearer understanding of children's development, emotional and behavioural difficulties, and the role of relationships in family life.
Accessible, scientifically grounded information can help parents recognise difficulties earlier, better understand their child's needs, and make more informed decisions about support.

I develop articles, educational materials, and resources for parents and families. I aim to present psychological information clearly, without simplifications that lose the complexity of real situations or promote universal solutions.
My perspective remains relational and integrative: the child is understood within their development, close relationships, and family system.

I also contribute to professional and public discussion of children's and families' mental health through podcasts, events, professional meetings, and psychoeducation initiatives. I aim to support a culture of prevention, professional responsibility, and collaboration between specialists, parents, and communities.

Another important direction is supporting students, psychologists, and psychotherapists in training or at the start of practice. My experience coordinating placements, facilitating peer consultation, and organising professional reflection spaces supports this work.
Professionals working with children and families need knowledge and techniques, but also safe contexts to think about cases, discuss difficulties, and learn together.

In the longer term, I want to develop education and prevention projects, professional resources, workshops, and collaborative spaces supporting families and specialists involved in children's development and mental health.
To learn more about the services I offer, visit Services. For questions or a possible collaboration, contact me through the website form.

professional.title: Training and professional experience
paragraphs: My professional training has developed through academic studies, long-term training, clinical experience, supervision, continuing professional development, and peer consultation.
I am licensed for autonomous practice in clinical psychology and psychotherapy by the Romanian College of Psychologists.

groups.title: Academic studies and long-term training
items: Bachelor's degree in Psychology, Faculty of Psychology and Education Sciences, Alexandru Ioan Cuza University, Iași, 2015–2018.
Long-term Integrative Psychotherapy training, Romanian Association for Integrative Psychotherapy (ARPI), Bucharest, 2018–2023.
Master's in Clinical Psychology and Child and Family Psychotherapy, Faculty of Psychology and Education Sciences, University of Bucharest, 2021–2023.
Long-term training in psychotherapy for children, adolescents, and the family system, APRICAS, started January 2026, currently ongoing.

groups.title: Professional experience
paragraphs: I have worked in psychology since 2019, developing experience in educational, social, clinical, and private-practice settings.
From October 2018 to June 2019, I accompanied and supported a girl with autism at school. From October 2019 to January 2020, I worked as an ABA behavioural therapist at Help Autism.
At FDP – Protagoniști în educație, I worked with children and families from disadvantaged backgrounds exposed to social and psychological risk factors.

From February 2020 to June 2021, as a psychological counsellor in the Social Sports School – Real Madrid Foundation project, I provided psychoeducation, prevention, and short-term psychological intervention with children and parents.
From September 2020 to June 2023, I worked as a clinical psychologist at the Wonder Day Centre. Activities included:
items: Initial and comprehensive psychological assessments using standardised instruments; assessment of children with special educational needs.
Individual and group counselling, and activities to prevent school dropout.
Workshops developing socio-emotional, relational, and social skills.
Psychological intervention and integrative psychotherapy adapted to children and families.
Work with circumstances involving trauma, neglect, abandonment, poverty, or other vulnerabilities.

paragraphs: In January 2022 I began private practice alongside my association work; from October 2022 it became my main professional activity.

In private practice I have provided clinical assessment, child and adolescent counselling, integrative psychotherapy, parent counselling, and intervention in parent–child relationships and family dynamics.

My clinical experience particularly concerns preschool and school-age children, adolescents, and their families, including emotional, behavioural, relational, adjustment, and developmental difficulties.

groups.title: Placements and formative experience
paragraphs: During my studies, placements and volunteering introduced me to different groups and perspectives on human development.
items: February–April 2016: preschool placement at Kindergarten no. 22, Iași.

July–September 2016: Erasmus+ placement at Istituto Figlie di Santa Maria della Provvidenza, Rome, with preschool children, people with disabilities, and older adults, including cognitive stimulation and rehabilitation.
February–May 2017: PSY PRO research project, coordinated by Professor Constantin Ticu, for the PsihoProfile psychometric testing platform.
May–June 2017: specialist placement at Socola Psychiatric Institute, Iași.
February–April 2019: Cariera PSY professional placement at Next Level – Integrative Counselling Solutions.
2021–2023: clinical placement in a private psychology practice during the master's programme.
Placement at Filaret Community Support Centre with homeless women, including clinical interviews, adult psychometric instruments, and experiential workshops supporting autonomy and social skills.

groups.title: Academic and social involvement
items: Active membership of E-team Psychology, supporting student academic events, public relations, and research/statistics projects.
Volunteering in a telephone support service for people at risk of suicide, at Sf. Damian Association.
Social activities for children admitted to an oncology hospital in Iași.

groups.title: Supervision and peer consultation
paragraphs: I consider supervision and peer consultation important components of responsible practice. Supervision supports analysis of the clinical process, professional boundaries, and understanding complex situations.
Peer consultation brings collegial perspectives, shared experience, and opportunities to reflect on practice with other professionals.

groups.title: Professional supervision
items: 100 hours of individual and group clinical psychology supervision with Andreea Abe Adebowale, December 2020–July 2023.
300 hours of integrative psychotherapy supervision through ARPI with Daniela Porumbu and Coralina Chiriac, December 2021–May 2023.
Additional monthly supervision for child, adolescent, and family cases with Andreea Abe Adebowale, 2024–2025.

groups.title: Participation in peer consultation groups
paragraphs: I have participated in several forms of professional peer consultation:
items: Interdisciplinary consultation with social-worker colleagues.
Consultation within the Terapeuți pentru copii și familii community alongside Andreea Abe Adebowale.
Monthly informal consultation with practice colleagues.
Groups with colleagues from ARPI training and supervision.
Groups focused on work with adult cases.

groups.title: Facilitating and co-creating peer consultation spaces
paragraphs: Alongside participating, I have organised, co-created, or facilitated spaces for reflection and professional support.
items: Online and in-person groups for specialists working with children and families.
Peer consultation within Mental Health Association.
Informal groups organised and facilitated by me.
The professional formats Șezătoarea Ideilor and Șezătoarea Emoțiilor.
Professional referral and resource-sharing groups.

paragraphs: These experiences developed my facilitation skills, understanding of group processes, and ability to build professional spaces based on safety, collaboration, and mutual respect.

groups.title: Continuing professional development
paragraphs: Continuing training is part of my professional responsibility and supports integrating current knowledge into assessment and intervention with children, adolescents, parents, and families. Selected directly relevant courses include:
items: Assessment and therapy of anxiety in children and adolescents, Andreea Abe Adebowale, 5 hours, 2025.
Divorce therapy with children and adolescents, Andreea Abe Adebowale, 2 hours, 2025.
Computerised psychological assessment of children and adolescents and the CogniKit platform, 55 hours, 2023.
Non-directive play interventions in child and family therapy, 2022.
Directive play interventions in child and family therapy, 2021.
Experiential assessment of the parent–child relationship, 2021.
Case conceptualisation and planning play-therapy interventions, 2021.
Training in the NEPSY developmental neuropsychological assessment battery, 2021.
